item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is preferable because its retry implementation can actually replay an os.File body after the first attempt, while B leaves the original request body closable and can therefore try to seek a closed file. Both patches materially violate the frozen API and scope contract, so A would still require substantial revision before merge.","reasons":["B's ensureReplayableBody sets GetBody but does not replace req.Body with a non-closing wrapper. For an *os.File, net/http can close the file after the first attempt, causing the retry's Seek to fail. B's test avoids this by using a wrapper around strings.Reader rather than the reported os.Open case.","A explicitly wraps the initial seekable body with io.NopCloser and tests retrying an *os.File, making its expanded retry behavior more credible.","A's Upload retry test uses content opened as an *os.File; B only tests Upload with strings.NewReader, so B does not verify the requested streamed-content scenario.","Both correctly buffer multipart data and validate empty filenames and nil readers, but neither tests source-reader failures as required."],"risks_a":["Upload has opts ...UploadFileOption instead of the exact required opts ...FilesOption signature.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's request and response behavior.","It adds prohibited association/custom-field APIs and NewFileWithFields machinery instead of using multipartbody.NewFile directly while preserving FilesOption behavior unchanged as required by the contract intent; it also changes option return types and global request/retry behavior beyond scope changes explicitly disallowed by the contract intent."],"risks_b":["Upload has opts ...UploadFileOption instead of opts ...FilesOption and calls Raw.Do instead of FilesService.Add.","Its seekable-body retry implementation is unsafe for the reported *os.File case because the first request may close the shared reader before GetBody seeks it.","It adds prohibited association APIs and NewFileWithFields machinery, while changing global retry behavior outside the requested scope changes explicitly disallowed by the contract intent."]}
